question: Should OpenClaw add native cross-gateway session-tool messaging in core, keep session tools gateway-local and expose plugin/MCP bridge seams, or defer this to the broader federation FRD?
rationale: The requested behavior is real and still missing, but it changes Gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message delivery, config, credentials, and security policy in a way automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Define Core Contract First
options.body: Define peer identity, authorization scopes, replay/idempotency, URL policy, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing core cross-gateway messaging.

options.title: Bridge Through Plugins Or MCP
options.body: Keep core session tools gateway-local and add only the missing extension seams needed for an external bridge or MCP integration to implement routing safely.

options.title: Fold Into Federation FRD
options.body: Pause this concrete session-tool implementation until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 resolves the broader bridge protocol and identity model.

recommendation.title: Define Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Define peer identity, authorization scopes, replay/idempotency, URL policy, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing core cross-gateway messaging.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses session-tool, Gateway config, and security-boundary surfaces where this owner candidate has the strongest current-main history signal.
